text:
Alex: heads up — seeing a regression in continuous batching when requests with tool/function calls and structured outputs hit stop tokens. decode pipeline stalls for ~30-60ms and we lose KV cache locality. attaching quick notes.

perf-bot: perf-alert: p95 decode latency increased by 12% on fleet r-12 over last deploy. sample ids: 87b2, 87b3, 87b4

Meera: can you paste a minimal repro or a profile snippet? is this across all models or a narrow family?

Alex: repro is small. happens mostly on mid-sized 13B variants when structured output + tool pauses used. profile:

```
timeline (shortened):
  t0: batch start (N=14)
  t0+6ms: token gen until stop token -> request A emits tool-call pause
  t0+6-40ms: runtime holds batch waiting for continuation (hold-window expired at 40ms)
  t0+42ms: resumed, but KV cache for request B evicted -> extra ~8ms KV refill
  result: tail latency + queuing -> p95 bump
```

Jon: hmm. so two mechanics colliding: batch formation is optimistic (assumes no long pauses), and KV cache eviction policy is LRU-ish with small per-shard budget. tool-call pauses force early flush and then later resume causes misses. also kernel choice for short sequences sometimes picks a higher-throughput kernel with larger setup cost which hurts resumed short continuations.

Sylvia: agree. quick ideas:
- bias batcher to prefer homogenous "no-toolcall" groups, but for requests with high tool-call probability either 1) isolate into small "paused" buckets or 2) extend hold-window for those requests.
- give per-request metadata: expected_toolcall_prob (from router/predictor) so batcher can make decisions.
- tweak KV cache soft-reserve to keep recent request contexts for up to X ms if they are flagged as likely to resume.

Meera: +1. we should avoid blindly extending global hold-window (regresses throughput). better to add a per-request hold hint and have queue policy respect token budget targets.

Alex: proposed experiment:
```
# config flags
continuous_batching.per_request_hold_hint = true
continuous_batching.hold_hint_ms = 80  # only for flagged requests
batcher.sampling.field = expected_toolcall_prob
kv_cache.soft_reserve_ms = 120
kernel.selection.short_seq_overhead_threshold = 4ms
```
Run A/B on r-12 for 2h.

Eva: I can run the canary. will add a tiny predictor to scoring service to emit expected_toolcall_prob (0.0-1.0) using heuristic: presence of json schema + function call likelihood from client header.

Jon: also collect these metrics in the profiler: per-request KV hit/miss, kernel-switch count, resumed-token-latency, and batch-formation-size-dist.

perf-bot: experiment template created: exp-1862345678-kv-tool-hold. rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 100% if p95 decode latency <= baseline+3% and throughput >= baseline-1%.

Sylvia: watch for unintended side-effects: increasing hold for flagged requests could allow malicious clients to monopolize KV slots; we need a per-user quota.

Alex: good point. add per-customer hold_budget and evict-by-age+priority. also add a safety that if resumed continuation not seen within 2x hold_hint_ms, we release KV immediately.

Meera: small additional thought: kernel selection tweak — prefer low-setup-cost kernel for resumed short continuations even if throughput slightly lower. saves tail.

Jon: agrees, but we need microbenchmarks. I'll run kernel-switch microbench on c4 and c8 configs and post numbers.

Eva: running canary now (5%). posting logs shortly.

perf-bot: canary update @5m: no crash, p95 decode on canary cohort +4.2% (above threshold). reverting to 0% pending analysis.

Alex: thanks. looks like hold_hint_ms=80 too aggressive. try smaller: 30ms and kv.soft_reserve_ms=80. also reduce predictor threshold to only flag >0.7.

Meera: agree. also instrument sampled request traces to see the distribution of actual pause durations — we might be able to use a small predictive distribution instead of a binary flag.

Sylvia: I'll add safety limits for per-customer KV-reserve and an abort path if observed abuse.

Eva: rerunning with new params now.

perf-bot: update @45m: canary p95 delta +0.9%, throughput -0.2%. KV hit-rate improved by 6% on resumed continuations. kernel-switch count decreased.

Alex: this is promising. next steps: run 2h A/B, collect perf traces, and Jon do kernel microbench. if stable, prepare rollout with per-customer quotas.

Jon: uploading microbench results to artifacts: median setup cost for low-overhead kernel = 1.8ms vs 4.9ms for high-throughput kernel on resumed seqs.

Meera: great. can we codify heuristic: if resumed_tokens_expected <= 16 -> pick low-setup kernel; else high-throughput. add a tunable threshold.

Sylvia: adding to rollout checklist: abuse detection, quota enforcement, metrics dashboard for KV-reserve usage.

Alex: thanks all. I'll open a short PR with the batcher changes + config flags and link the canary results. tagging @Meera @Jon for review.

Eva: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/7321

Meera: reviewing.

Jon: will follow up with kernel perf numbers in the PR.

Sylvia: moving to the post-mortem board to track next ops items. :white_check_mark:

Alex: end — thanks team :thumbsup:
